question: In what duration will a sum of money double itself at 20% per annum simple interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
To **double** a sum, the **Interest** must be equal to 100% of the **Principal**.

Time (T) = 100 ÷ Rate of Interest (R)

T = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 years

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38d29f50335ded5951cfcdf7c2e0f9da36b0a82e052afd9f07deff09b0c541dd.png] 
**Given:**

Let the **Principal** (P) = ₹100

Since the sum **doubles** itself, **Amount** (A) = 2 × 100 = ₹200

**Simple Interest** (SI) = A − P = 200 − 100 = ₹100

**Rate of Interest** (R) = 20%

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 100 = (100 × 20 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 20 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 20

⇒ T = 5 years

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplier Method for Simple Interest

If a sum becomes 'n' times in 'T' years, the relation is (n − 1) = (R × T) ÷ 100.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is always calculated on the **original principal**, whereas in Compound Interest, it is calculated on the **accumulated amount**.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total percentage of interest earned over 'T' years at 'R%' rate is simply R × T %.
